title: 101 steps 4 to 6: the faces, the lens and the street layer (Latch, 0.2.287)
sub: Latch, 2026-11-09 · build 0.2.287 (out/build/play/The Suborned.app, the old town; draw check ok; the captures are 0.2.286's, the same HUD) · Sky's mix (2026-11-08): street labels top right, tokens bottom right; steps 4 to 6 follow Glyph's S mocks (briefs/101/glyph/r2/S-*.png). Each moment below is the real frame beside the mock at the same moment, with how much of the screen the HUD takes. Pictures: briefs/101/latch/r4/ (git-ignored).

body: Step 4, the roster as street faces (HudToolkit.Faces.cs):
No tray: each agent is its live portrait (60 px) in a cream ring over a soft shadow; the selected one ringed turquoise 5 px out; the others no longer dim.
Health is a column of pips at the face's right, turquoise, cream once lost, each in an ink keyline; a hit flashes the lost pip; badly hurt, they pulse.
What the agent is doing is one icon on a disc at the face's lower right: the act, a queued order, a landing's tone, the armed verb; firing, the disc is orange. No seconds, no bar.
The sidearm mark sits at the lower left while drawn, or on the selected or hovered face; a click draws or holsters; its hover opens the stance fan.
A known face's badge at the upper left, the watcher's eye at the upper right; the cue layer (spikes under fire, rays firing) as before.
A refused order's why, an under-fire cause, or a word the icon can't say ('too far', '→ Inez', a landing's word) is a street label beside the face.

Every click kept: the face selects, Shift adds, a drag carries; the act disc switches a walk's pace; its × stops the act on hover; the Squad tab under the faces (third person names the way back beside it).
Retired: the tall column (its art, the row under each face, the steel dividers and their audit) and the busy chips beside it.

Step 5, the scope as a round lens (HudToolkit.Scope.cs, Keys096.cs, Sight.cs): 146 px of dark glass in the bottom left, a cream rim, the block's light parts on it, the north wedge on the rim, and its three round tabs on the rim (turn left, the cones eye, turn right). One scale keeps the whole block inside the lens at every yaw. It retires the 212 x 132 plate.
Step 6, the street layer:
Speech (HudToolkit.Bubbles.cs): a cream bubble, fully round, the speaker's face or badge at its left, Barlow 15.5 in ink, a fine cream stem to the head.

A report about to land (HudToolkit.OnWay.cs): an orange disc with the way's icon over the reporter (ringed turquoise while it can still be stopped), the seconds in orange street type beside it, and a ring at his feet draining over the last 10 s.
Our car (HudToolkit.StepMarks.cs): the lock and the holders' count laid on the car as street type, and the five seat pips in ink keylines, no backing pill.
A holder's mark: a struck disc in his signal colour (amber police and guards, violet rivals); the rival car's hold words as a street label.

The target (HudToolkit.TargetRings.cs, Lock.cs): the focus ring in his signal colour, whole in range, three arcs for a long shot; a shield on its front while his cover counts against our shooters (the engine's own cover rule); his health pips in his signal colour; the lock reticle is a crosshair on the street, no disc; why it waits is a street label.

The hover label (HudToolkit.Pill.cs): what a click or hold does, as street labels with no plate: the act's disc (harm: the light disc; a shot: the crosshair), the head word in soft ink, the words in ink, the doers' faces, 'Watched spot' in orange. The hold fills a turquoise ring round the disc.

The first shot's row: under the label while the right hold charges, Fable's 'Goes loud' on an orange pill, the Alert lamps it reaches, the police badge, the seal's lock and the Trail. Never a hit chance or a time.
Off screen (HudToolkit.Edges.cs): Popovic's face, the cell's and the key people's at the screen's edge, each in a cream ring with an ink chevron pointing out.

The rivals-follow card (HostCrucial.cs): when our car drives off, the three posted rivals going after it are a news card reading book.feed.cards.rivals-follow (Fable's 'Rivals after our car'). With no words the card isn't made at all. It ranks with the rivals for our car.

The Mislead tip (HostQuiet.cs, HostConvo.Lines.cs): arrive/mislead is in HostQuiet's scene list, and the Mislead's own scene opens with the Scout's tip (an arrival line alone is history, never a bubble); her report after it stays quiet. Fable's tips are in the words now.

Files: HudToolkit.cs 1279 → 1274 lines, HudToolkit.Less.cs 1794 → 1378 (the bubbles, the end-step marks and the edge marks moved out); both shrank; every new file is under 500 (the largest, HudToolkit.StepMarks.cs, 244), and PlayText.cs (597) is untouched.

sections.h: What stays in the old kit (not in steps 4 to 6)
body: The loop and watcher window markers (the plate with the eye and its time), the attention clocks, the refusal pops, the paused plan's ghosts, the seen count, the cancel tag, the why list, the act ring and its wedges, the door and car step markers, Inez's person card, the shooters' cameos in their chrome ring.

The report's ring is neutral, not orange: the play grade turns an orange ground mark into the cones' red (sampled 224, 0, 0), and the signal pass outside the grade draws over legs. The orange stays on its disc and seconds.
Outside a fight the hover never offers Fire (brief 067), so the 'Goes loud' row shows while the right hold charges; the r101 proof pictures it.

Run full (098's geometry commit asked for the world steps), then the delta of the last fixes on the final build. The working tree moved under it: Fable's sweep landed (b451d1083, d7d83de8c, 41a15e4db) and the engine DLL was re-copied, so the batch's last build is 0.2.286. 0.2.287 is 0.2.286 with one reader moved to a smaller file (Fable's 'Goes loud' out of PlayText.cs, which is over 500 lines): draw check ok in 8.4 s, r101 ok (its first-shot row read through the moved reader), host logic 180/180, typecheck clean, words ok.
sim ok: 472/472 headless scenarios replay identically.
words ok (after pinning 'Let go' for ProofHold.cs: the sweep's new lines 'Let go of me…' and 'Let go! Get back…' made the pill's own head word a text.json word).
compile ok; host logic 180/180 (the new rivals-follow case and the Mislead case included); kit ok; world ok.
unity-world ok (692 s: the harbour district, then the old town swap, verify, host and bake); unity-match 571/571.
game-build 0.2.286 with the full proof: every section ok but r083, whose r085insetEveryLine failed in company; game-check reran r083 alone: ok; scenarios 472/472.

r083's two inset checks are flaky timing checks (two of the guard's docked lines in 8 s): on one build (0.2.283) one run passed both and two failed route A; HEAD's words in the app failed the same way, so neither the sweep nor this round's code is the cause.
shots ok (13 in 23 s).

budget FAILED: shots 11/11 within budget, layout audit 10/11, proof sets r059 14/14, r067 30/32, r123 6/7, r083 2/2. What's left isn't this round's: the news lozenge's line with the sweep's longer why ('the square's mast camera saw the Fixer stay too long beside the café · 2:46', 430 px in its 296 px box, shown with an ellipsis); the next key event's two-word names plus a time over the marker cap ('Turn driver by 5:20', 'Popovic exits 5:30', known since round 3); Inez's person card beside the lozenge (2 card panels).
late-fight ok: loud-fight worst 30.2 ms at the tail (tick 3122), p99 8.3 ms, mean 5.9 ms; loud-left-downed worst 28.5 ms, p99 9.7 ms (a noisy machine: load about 10 on 18 cores).

tp-long FAILED on the world, not the HUD: third person 6.4 and 8.4 M triangles (limit 6 M), shadow casters 1,273 and 1,386 (limit 1,200), renderers past 150 m 1,627 and 1,507 (limit 1,500); the play view 3.9 ms mean, p99 5.4 ms, 1.3 M triangles. It failed the same way in the last full batch on file (0.2.164, 6.9 M).
perf064 not run (opt-in). No Air run: that needs Sky's OK.

The full test suite: 2725 pass, 8 fail, none in the HUD or the host: the levels skyline tests, the scratch-copy end-to-end, Inez's rounds on the drawn floor (tools/geometry/legs.test.ts) and the recorded routes' ticks (tools/routines/rounds.test.ts). The game tools' own tests 308/308.
Play zoom at the Air's 2880 x 1864 (the proof's proxy, not the Air's GPU): 250.1 fps mean, p99 5.7 ms.
Play zoom at 1920 x 1080 (the shots): 250.7 fps mean, p99 7 ms; start-overhead-day 255 fps, p99 5.9 ms, GPU 3.5 ms.
The slowest of the proof's seven spots: fire-commander 67.6 fps, p99 10.8 ms (60 fps needs p99 under 16.7 ms).

The HUD's cost: plain elements, labels and sprites; no painter on the faces; keyline copies set only when their words change; the rings in the world-mesh batch. The roster sets its styles only when its state changes (the sidearm's look, the pips' layout).

Fable: the why shorts that lead the news lozenge's line want to fit about 40 characters (the sweep's 'the square's mast camera saw the Fixer stay too long beside the café' is 67), or the lozenge shows them clipped.

Glyph and Splice: the next key event's names over the marker cap (from round 3); Inez's person card beside the lozenge in r123; the pieces still in the old kit (above); whether the report's neutral ring reads well enough.

Splice: the proofmap rows for the new files (Pill with ActMark's sections; Bubbles, StepMarks and Edges with Less's) and r101 on HostActivity's and HostHold's rows; r083's inset timing checks (8 s windows) flake under load.
Vela and Datum: tp-long's third-person triangle, caster and far-renderer counts.
Pulse and Keel: the routines and geometry tests that fail (Inez's rounds, the recorded routes' ticks).
Sky: an Air run when you want one (not started).
